capabilities.name: docs/ tree layout and section _meta.json contract
capabilities.behavior: docs/ has 7 section dirs, each with exactly one _meta.json: adr, concepts, contract, daily-use, dev, mobile, troubleshooting. Schema is {"title": string, "pages": string[]}. Titles: adr="Architecture Decisions", concepts="Concepts", contract="API Contract", daily-use="Daily Use", dev="Developer Reference", mobile="Mobile App", troubleshooting="Troubleshooting". pages entries are basenames WITHOUT extension and resolve to .md or .mdx (mobile lists "status-icons" → status-icons.mdx). pages order is the rendered nav order and is curated, not alphabetical — dev is [instrumented-tests-ci, security-testing, dependency-updates, release-and-promotion, signing-and-secrets, spdx-header-policy, plugin-architecture, wear-os-architecture]. There is NO docs/_meta.json; section ordering/inclusion at the top level is decided in the consuming website repo, not here.
edge_cases: A page file present on disk but absent from its section's pages array is not in the nav.
No root docs/_meta.json exists, so this repo cannot order or name its own top-level sections.
pages arrays are hand-maintained: nothing in CI validates that every .md/.mdx is listed or that every listed page exists.

capabilities.name: Publication gate: what makes a page publishable
capabilities.behavior: Two conditions, both hand-enforced: (1) YAML frontmatter with `title:` and `description:` delimited by `---`; (2) the basename appearing in the owning directory's _meta.json pages array. All 18 pages inside the 7 section dirs satisfy both. The two files at docs/ root — history-extraction.md and THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md — have NO frontmatter and belong to no pages array, so they are repo-internal documents that are never published as website pages (THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md is instead consumed by the Gradle build). docs/licenses/*.txt are plain text, not pages. Frontmatter titles may be quoted when they contain a colon (all three ADRs quote theirs). Descriptions are one-sentence and used as the page subtitle/meta description.
edge_cases: No CI check enforces frontmatter presence or pages-array membership; a new page silently fails to publish.
No link checker exists — broken cross-references are undetected.

capabilities.name: Docs → website publication pipeline (notify-docs-update.yml)
capabilities.behavior: Workflow "Notify Website on Docs Update". Triggers: push to `main` touching `docs/**` or `.github/workflows/notify-docs-update.yml`, plus manual `workflow_dispatch` (documented as the way to force a rebuild after a failed run). Top-level and job-level `permissions: {}` (no GITHUB_TOKEN scopes at all). Single job `notify` on ubuntu-latest, two steps: (1) mint a cross-repo token with actions/create-github-app-token pinned to SHA 1b10c78c7865c340bc4f6099eb2f838309f1e8c3 (v3), app-id `secrets.CI_APP_ID`, private-key `secrets.CI_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`, `owner: github.repository_owner` (deliberately dynamic so org renames don't break it — the App installation lookup does not follow rename redirects), `repositories: website`; (2) `gh api repos/<owner>/website/dispatches -f event_type=docs-updated -F client_payload[source]=<repo> -F client_payload[sha]=<sha>`. The website repo pulls and renders the docs; this repo only fires the signal.
edge_cases: Only `main` publishes; docs merged to `develop` are invisible until promotion.
Dispatch is fire-and-forget: a failed website build is not surfaced here.
Nothing validates docs content before dispatch.

capabilities.name: Cross-repo shared docs namespace (relative links leave this repo)
capabilities.behavior: Published pages link with docs-root-relative paths to pages that do NOT exist in this repository: ../get-started.md, ../get-started.md#choose-your-path, ../get-started.md#a-note-on-the-terminal, ../troubleshooting/bg-not-updating.md, ../concepts/what-this-software-is-and-isnt.md, ../concepts/privacy.md, ../daily-use/dashboard.md, ./connecting-medtronic.md (CareLink page). This proves the website merges this repo's docs/ tree with the platform repo's docs/ tree into one namespace; a link is only resolvable post-merge. Conversely install.md links back into GitHub with absolute URLs for releases and ROADMAP.md. A Swift/iOS port that ships its own docs must reproduce this merged-tree assumption or rewrite every relative link.
edge_cases: install.md links to ./status-icons.md but the file is status-icons.mdx — extension-tolerant resolution assumed.

Repo slugs are inconsistent across documents: GlycemicGPT/GlycemicGPT, GlycemicGPT/android-unofficial, GlycemicGPT/glycemicgpt-android-unofficial, lumose-health/GlycemicGPT, lumose-health/.github, lumose-health/android-unofficial all appear.

capabilities.name: MDX pages with inline JSX (status-icons.mdx)
capabilities.behavior: docs/mobile/status-icons.mdx is the only .mdx page. It embeds raw <svg> elements with JSX attribute syntax (viewBox, fill, aria-hidden, style={{verticalAlign:"-4px",marginRight:"8px"}}) inline in prose, so the site renderer must support MDX/JSX, not just CommonMark. It documents the home-screen status row: Bluetooth pump state (blue #2563eb solid = Connected; amber #d97706 = Scanning…/Connecting…/Reconnecting…; red #dc2626 crossed-out = No pump connected/Pairing failed, explicitly documented as the resting non-error state); sync status (up/down arrows = Synced, amber cloud-check = Pending, red = Not synced/Sync error); server reachability (blue cloud-check = Reachable, no label; red = "Backend unreachable"; red = "Offline"). Sync and reachability icons are hidden entirely in BLE-only mode (no server configured). Integration brand marks follow, at most one pump mark (Tandem or Medtronic) plus data sources (Nightscout); unbranded plugins show no mark; the mark row scrolls horizontally.
edge_cases: Two separate icons intentionally answer different questions ("is my data uploaded" vs "can I reach the server right now") and must not look alike.

capabilities.name: docs/mobile/install.md — published Android install contract
capabilities.behavior: Requirements: Android 11+ (API 30+), Bluetooth, a reachable platform URL (http://<lan-ip>:3000 local, or https://domain). Explicit statement: "Today only Android is supported. iOS is on the roadmap … but not available yet" — iPhone users get browser dashboard only. Distribution: signed `app-release.apk` from the topmost GitHub release WITHOUT the yellow Pre-release label; dev users take `app-debug.apk` from the `dev-latest` pre-release. Install Path A = tap APK, toggle "Allow from this source". Path B = `adb install app-release.apk` after enabling Developer Options (tap Build number 7×) and USB debugging; `INSTALL_FAILED_USER_RESTRICTED` means policy-blocked (work device). Onboarding = Server URL then email/password sign-in. Pairing: Bluetooth + Location permission (Android requires Location for BLE scan; app does not track location), pump into pairing mode, 6-digit code. Battery impact documented as <5%/day. No auto-update; stale-version banner; in-place APK upgrade preserves settings/login/pairing.
edge_cases: Tandem pumps allow exactly one BLE connection at a time — must unpair t:connect first.
Battery optimization must be disabled or the background pump link drops.
"If the dashboard is still empty after 5 minutes" is the documented troubleshooting threshold.

capabilities.name: docs/mobile/wear-os.md — published watch install contract
capabilities.behavior: Watch face is optional. Two components: `wear-device` (companion app providing complications) and `watchface` (Watch Face Format APK). Wear OS 6+: ADB-install `wear-device-release.apk` once, then the phone app pushes the face via the Watch Face Push API (Settings → Watch → Push watch face). Wear OS 5: ADB-install BOTH `wear-device-release.apk` and `watchface-release.apk`; phone cannot push. Version check at Settings → System → About → Versions. Dev mode: tap Build number 7×, enable ADB debugging + Debug over Wi-Fi/Bluetooth; watch shows `<ip>:<port>` e.g. 192.168.1.42:5555; `adb connect`, `adb devices`, `adb -s <serial> install`, `-r` to upgrade in place. Face renders glucose, trend arrow (up/down/flat), IoB, time; updates once per glucose reading interval (~5 minutes). Documented failure threshold: `--` for glucose >5 minutes after fresh setup. Face is explicitly read-only.
edge_cases: Wear OS forbids APK download from the watch browser, forcing the ADB workflow — called out as the hardest step in the whole product.
Roadmap items (Watch Face Push expansion, possible Play Store distribution) are documented as not available.

capabilities.name: docs/troubleshooting/cant-pair-pump.md
capabilities.behavior: Only page in the troubleshooting section here. Prerequisites checklist: Bluetooth on, Location permission granted (OS requirement for BLE scan), pump in pairing mode (Tandem: Options → Bluetooth Settings → Pair Device), pump within a couple of meters, both batteries healthy. Pump 6-digit code "times out after a couple of minutes". Ordering rule: app must be scanning BEFORE the pump starts advertising (cancel pairing → force-stop app → reopen → tap Pair pump → then pair on pump). One-BLE-connection-at-a-time rule for Tandem; unpair t:connect. Requires Android 11+ (API 30+). Drop-after-connect causes: battery optimization (set Don't optimize; Samsung also has a "Sleeping apps" list), pump BLE flake (power cycle, wait 10 seconds), metal/magnetic phone cases. Tandem Mobi is protocol-compatible but unverified on hardware — "at your own risk".
edge_cases: Explicit log-redaction warning before posting to Discord: emails, bearer/API tokens, auth headers, account IDs, pump serials, BLE device identifiers must be replaced with [REDACTED] or DM'd to a maintainer.

capabilities.name: docs/daily-use/connecting-medtronic-pump.md
capabilities.behavior: Covers MiniMed 680G/770G/780G on-device BLE pairing, explicitly beta and read-only. Contrasts with CareLink cloud sync (separate, unrelated path). Pairing is advertise-and-wait, inverted from Tandem: the PHONE advertises as a BLE peripheral named exactly "Mobile 000001" and the PUMP initiates. Flow states named in the doc: waiting → connecting → connected. Pump pairs with only one phone at a time; must be removed from MiniMed Mobile first. Reads sensor glucose, IoB, basal (active rate), bolus history, reservoir, battery. Documented limitation: SmartGuard auto-basal micro-boluses are "not yet fully attributed". IoB is read as the pump exposes it and has been confirmed against a live 780G's on-screen Active Insulin, subject to display rounding. Named failure copy: "No pump has connected yet.", "This phone can't act as a Bluetooth accessory.", "Couldn't start Bluetooth advertising.", "The secure handshake timed out" / "the pump rejected the secure handshake."
edge_cases: Some phones cannot act as a BLE peripheral at all — hard blocker with dedicated error copy.
Pairing is remembered; reconnect is automatic when back in range.

capabilities.name: docs/concepts/acknowledgments.md — attribution posture (Tandem vs Medtronic)
capabilities.behavior: Public credit page. Draws the load-bearing distinction: Tandem = ARCHITECTURAL REFERENCE ONLY. jwoglom/pumpX2 (MIT, James Woglom) and jwoglom/controlX2 (MIT) were studied; the Kotlin driver is an independent port; no code imported; pumpX2 test vectors are used only to validate parser correctness. In-source headers cite upstream MIT in TandemProtocol.kt, JpakeAuthenticator.kt, EcJpake.kt, Hkdf.kt. Medtronic = DIRECT DEPENDENCY/PORT and "the one place GlycemicGPT differs from its Tandem posture": org.openminimed:javasake is a Maven Central runtime dependency driven through MedtronicSakeSession; PythonPumpConnector's CGM, IDD-status, history, device-info and battery readers are ported line-for-line; PythonSake and JavaPumpConnector informed the connection manager. Legal basis: OpenMinimed is GPL-3.0 and this app is GPL-3.0, with explicit permission from palmarci (Pál Marci) who relicensed for this purpose. Also credits drfubar, Morten Fyhn Amundsen, Stenium, @planiitis (medtronic-bt-decrypt PoC).
edge_cases: Page invites correction issues explicitly: "correctness matters more than concision".
Also credits the diabetes-OSS movement: Nightscout, OpenAPS/Dana Lewis, Loop/LoopKit/Pete Schwamb, AndroidAPS, xDrip+, Tidepool — and states GlycemicGPT does not do closed-loop "and never will".

capabilities.name: docs/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md — scope rule and content
capabilities.behavior: Records SOURCE LINEAGE only: upstream projects whose protocol work was studied, ported, or derived from. It explicitly is NOT the redistributed-dependency list ("do not expand this document into a runtime-dependency list") because a hand-maintained list goes stale on the next bump; that obligation is discharged by the generated attribution shown under "Redistributed Components". Sections: Tandem (pumpX2, controlX2 — MIT, full MIT text reproduced); Medtronic/OpenMinimed (GPL-3.0, four-repo table mapping PythonSake/PythonPumpConnector/JavaSake/JavaPumpConnector to their role, note that firmware-derived SAKE key material ships in the JavaSake artifact under GPL-3.0 and introduces no new secret); EC-JPAKE (particle-iot/ecjpake-java, Apache-2.0, Copyright 2022 Particle Industries, full Apache-2.0 text minus the instructional APPENDIX); SQLCipher (net.zetetic:sqlcipher-android:4.13.0, BSD-3-Clause, ZETETIC LLC, full text) — the documented example of a component that is both a lineage entry and a runtime dependency.
edge_cases: This file is compiled into the APK verbatim and gated by a unit test, so any edit is an app change (see android.yml path filter).
It is not a published website page (no frontmatter, no pages entry).

capabilities.name: docs/licenses/ — canonical license text bundle
capabilities.behavior: Nine .txt files, one per license identifier, consumed by the Gradle attribution generator: Apache-2.0.txt (202 lines), BouncyCastle.txt (7), BSD-2-Clause.txt (9), BSD-3-Clause.txt (11), CUP.txt (19), ICU.txt (12), MIT.txt (18), SAX-PD-2.0.txt (10), SAX-PD.txt (31). Filename-without-extension IS the lookup key: `docs/licenses/<identifier>.txt`. Seven are SPDX identifiers; BouncyCastle and CUP are bundled-by-name because their POMs declare no SPDX identifier and their artifacts ship no license text. GPL-3.0 is NOT here — the repo-root LICENSE is the GPL-3.0 source and is shipped as its own asset. BSD-2/BSD-3/MIT texts carry `<year> <owner>` placeholders (canonical SPDX templates, not per-component instantiations).
edge_cases: A license family with no matching .txt fails the build (see generator failure modes).

capabilities.name: generateDependencyAttribution Gradle task
capabilities.behavior: @CacheableTask in app/build.gradle.kts. Reads Licensee `artifacts.json` reports from four AttributionSource triples: (:app, licenseeAndroidRelease, releaseRuntimeClasspath), (:wear-device, licenseeAndroidRelease, releaseRuntimeClasspath), (:watchface, licenseeAndroidDigitalFullRelease, digitalFullReleaseRuntimeClasspath), (:watchface, licenseeAndroidAnalogMechanicalRelease, analogMechanicalReleaseRuntimeClasspath). Uses evaluationDependsOn per sibling project (accepted cost: not configuration-cache compatible) because siblings are applications, not consumable dependencies. Resolves artifacts through an artifactView filtered to ModuleComponentIdentifier (published archives only; project deps are this repo's own GPL-3.0 modules). Resolution is strict — no lenient view — so a failed artifact breaks the build rather than dropping a NOTICE. Outputs to build/generated/attribution: runtime_dependencies.md and runtime_dependency_licenses.txt. licenseTexts input = rootProject docs/licenses.
edge_cases: Empty component list → GradleException ("would ship empty, which reads as 'this app redistributes nothing'").
Component with no SPDX identifier and no entry in unmappedLicenses/unreproducedLicenses → GradleException naming the coordinates.
A license identifier with no docs/licenses/<id>.txt → GradleException listing the missing families.

capabilities.name: Attribution generator output format
capabilities.behavior: runtime_dependencies.md: `# Redistributed Components`, three fixed preamble paragraphs, then `Components: <N>.`, then one `## <heading>` per license family sorted alphabetically. Heading = the component's FIRST license identifier, or the literal `License terms available elsewhere` for unreproduced ones. Each entry: "- `group:artifact:version` -- <name> -- carries a NOTICE" (name omitted when blank or equal to coordinates; the NOTICE suffix only when that component contributed one), then an indented scm URL line, then "Also licensed under: X, Y" for multi-license components, then "Terms: <note>". runtime_dependency_licenses.txt: header "LICENSE TEXTS AND UPSTREAM NOTICES", then per identifier a 64-'=' separator line, the identifier, another separator, the bundled text; then a final "UPSTREAM NOTICES" block with per-component "--- coordinates ---" sections. Components are keyed by coordinates so the four variant reports de-duplicate.
edge_cases: Multi-license components (xml-apis = Apache-2.0 plus two SAX public-domain grants) get ALL their texts bundled but are grouped under the first only.
License texts must never reach the markdown renderer — numbered clauses parse as list markers, indented lines as code blocks.

capabilities.name: NOTICE harvesting (Apache-2.0 §4(d) discharge)
capabilities.behavior: collectNotices() scans every resolved .jar/.aar artifact. NOTICE_ENTRY regex is `(META-INF/)?NOTICE(\.(txt|md))?` with IGNORE_CASE, fully anchored — so `META-INF/notices/other/NOTICE` is deliberately NOT matched, because a nested path belongs to a bundled dependency and is that dependency's obligation, not this project's. For an .aar the nested `classes.jar` is opened as a ZipInputStream and its own NOTICE entries harvested too. Multiple notices within one archive are sorted by entry name and joined with a blank line. Empty/whitespace notices are dropped. Any archive that cannot be read as a zip throws GradleException ("Could not read <archive> while collecting notices") rather than silently dropping attribution. Notices map is sorted by coordinates. LicenseAssetsTest asserts jakarta.inject:jakarta.inject-api (pulled by Hilt) appears as a stable witness.
edge_cases: A component whose artifact path is not in artifactsByCoordinates falls back to the bare filename as its label.
Five of six reproduced NOTICE files are reachable only through :wear-device, which is why :app alone is insufficient.

capabilities.name: Licensee allowlist policy (root build.gradle.kts)
capabilities.behavior: Applied to every subproject with the app.cash.licensee plugin, declared once at root so the three APK modules cannot disagree. unusedAction(IGNORE) because one policy spans three different graphs. allow(): Apache-2.0, MIT, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, ICU, SAX-PD, SAX-PD-2.0. allowUrl(): https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-3.0.txt ("GPL-3.0-only, the same licence this application ships under"), http://opensource.org/licenses/BSD-2-Clause (commonmark 0.13.0 predates SPDX in its POM). allowDependency() with a `because` reason, per exact version: play-services-base 18.5.0, play-services-basement 18.4.0, play-services-tasks 18.2.0, play-services-wearable 18.2.0; six twelvemonkeys 3.9.4 artifacts; edu.princeton.cup:java-cup:10k; net.zetetic:sqlcipher-android:4.13.0; org.bouncycastle:bcprov-jdk18on:1.84; com.github.jeziellago:Markwon:58aa5aba6a; com.github.jeziellago:compose-markdown:0.5.8; com.github.xgouchet:AXML:v1.0.1. A version bump re-raises the judgement rather than inheriting it.
edge_cases: DELIBERATE OMISSION: EPL-1.0 is intentionally absent — the FSF considers it incompatible with GPLv3 for a combined distributed work. The one EPL-1.0 artifact that reached the graph (an XPath 2.0 processor, transitive of the alpha wear watchface validator) is excluded at that dependency in wear-device/build.gradle.kts; WatchFaceValidatorTest proves the validator still works without it. Any new EPL dependency fails the gate rather than shipping.

capabilities.name: Unmapped and unreproduced license maps
capabilities.behavior: unmappedRuntimeLicenses (coordinates → license text to use when the POM declares no SPDX id): Markwon:58aa5aba6a→Apache-2.0, compose-markdown:0.5.8→Apache-2.0, AXML:v1.0.1→Apache-2.0 (JitPack POMs carry no license metadata); six twelvemonkeys 3.9.4 artifacts→BSD-3-Clause (POM says the unmapped name "The BSD License"); three commonmark 0.13.0 artifacts→BSD-2-Clause (declared by URL); bcprov-jdk18on:1.84→BouncyCastle; java-cup:10k→CUP. unreproducedRuntimeLicenses (coordinates → note on where the terms live): the four play-services artifacts → "Android Software Development Kit License -- https://developer.android.com/studio/terms"; sqlcipher-android:4.13.0 → "BSD-style Zetetic licence, reproduced in full under Third-Party Licenses above"; org.openminimed:javasake:0.2.0 → "GNU General Public License v3.0 -- the license this application ships under; its full text is the GPL-3.0 document in this screen". Fallback order: declared SPDX → unmapped override → external note → build failure.
edge_cases: The override is consulted ONLY when the POM declared no SPDX identifier — a declared identifier always wins.
A component that is neither SPDX-declared nor classified is surfaced as a build failure, never papered over with an "undeclared" placeholder.

capabilities.name: generateLicenseAssets Gradle task — the five shipped assets
capabilities.behavior: @CacheableTask producing assets/licenses/ inside every variant (wired via androidComponents.onVariants → addGeneratedSourceDirectory, with a checkNotNull that fails loudly if a variant has no asset source, because a variant that lost it would ship an APK with no license text and only debug is unit-tested). Five files: project_license_notice.md (the README `## License` section, heading included, verbatim, up to the next `## `), third_party_licenses.md (docs/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md whole), gpl-3.0.txt (repo-root LICENSE whole), runtime_dependencies.md and runtime_dependency_licenses.txt (from generateDependencyAttribution). Nothing is rewritten for display — normalisation belongs to the UI — so each asset stays an exact substring of its source and the drift test is a plain equality check. Regenerated on every build, so documents are the single source of truth.
edge_cases: Any whole-file source that is blank → GradleException ("Refusing to ship an APK whose licence screen would show a blank section in its place").
README.md missing a `## License` heading → GradleException naming the heading.
This check runs for EVERY variant, whereas LicenseAssetsTest only gates variants that run unit tests.

capabilities.name: In-app license viewer (LicensesScreen) — REQUIRED product surface
capabilities.behavior: Reached from Settings → App Info card → "Open Source Licenses" TextButton (testTag open_source_licenses_button) → nav route "licenses", title "Open Source Licenses", Icons.Default.Description. DetailScaffold with back. State machine: Loading (CircularProgressIndicator) → Loaded | Unavailable. Unavailable shows "License text could not be read from this build." in error color and is documented as a packaging failure, not a user state (triggered only by IOException reading assets; logged via Timber). Loaded renders one SelectionContainer wrapping a LazyColumn (contentPadding 16.dp, spacedBy 12.dp, testTag licenses_content): project notice → divider → third-party → dividers around one item per redistributed-component license family → one item per license-text paragraph → one item per GPL paragraph. rememberLazyListState is hoisted above the Loading branch so rotation returns the reader to position rather than the top of a 35 KB document. Assets are read on Dispatchers.IO; no connectivity required.
edge_cases: GPL and license-text documents are rendered as PLAIN TEXT, never markdown: numbered clauses parse as list markers and indented lines as code blocks.
Paragraph split regex is `\n\s*\n`; per-paragraph items exist so the list measures only on-screen paragraphs instead of ~670 GPL lines.

capabilities.name: License viewer markdown normalisation
capabilities.behavior: stripUnresolvableLinks: regex `(?` before rendering (blocks outbound image fetches), and onLinkClicked only opens links whose lowercase form starts with https:// or http://. The license screen passes linkifyMask = 0 because these documents name files, not sites (Linkify.WEB_URLS would turn `some-file.md` into a link), and isTextSelectable = true because the markdown view is outside SelectionContainer's reach.
edge_cases: AppMarkdownText returns early on blank markdown, rendering nothing.

capabilities.name: LicenseAssetsTest — license drift gate
capabilities.behavior: Robolectric test reading assets back out of the built variant and comparing to `../<path>` on disk. Assertions: FULL_LICENSE == repo LICENSE verbatim; THIRD_PARTY == docs/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md verbatim; full license contains "GNU GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE" and "Version 3, 29 June 2007" and length > 30,000; third-party contains "# Third-Party Licenses" and length > 10,000; project notice length > 200, starts with "## License", is a verbatim substring of README.md, contains no later `\n## ` (over-capture guard), and contains both "Copyright (C) 2026 Josh Engelbrecht" and "GPL-3.0-only". Component asset must start with "# Redistributed Components" and name okhttp, retrofit, room-runtime, timber, sentry-android, kotlinx-coroutines-core, plus wear-only androidx.wear.watchface:watchface-push. License-text asset must contain "Apache License"/"Version 2.0, January 2004", a non-blank UPSTREAM NOTICES block containing "\n--- " and jakarta.inject:jakarta.inject-api. BouncyCastle and CUP bodies must each exceed 200 chars.
edge_cases: SPDX_FAMILIES_WITH_TEXT = {Apache-2.0, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, ICU, MIT, SAX-PD, SAX-PD-2.0}; NON_SPDX_HEADINGS = {BouncyCastle, CUP, License terms available elsewhere}. Any heading outside those two sets fails the test.
play-services-base's own entry must carry "Terms: Android Software Development Kit License" — checked per-entry, not per-heading.
Section-split count must equal (number of `## ` lines) + 1.

capabilities.name: CI treats license documents as app code
capabilities.behavior: android.yml's detect-changes job (dorny/paths-filter pinned to 7b450fff21473bca461d4b92ce414b9d0420d706 / v4.0.2) gates the whole Android build on an `android` filter. Beyond app/, wear-device/, watchface/, plugins/, gradle/, gradlew(.bat), settings.gradle.kts, settings-gradle.lockfile, build.gradle.kts, gradle.properties and the workflow itself, the filter deliberately includes README.md, LICENSE, docs/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md and docs/licenses/** — "a change to one of these is an app change even though it is a document". Other docs/** changes skip the build entirely. Additionally app/build.gradle.kts registers ../README.md, ../LICENSE, ../docs/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md, ../docs/licenses (dir) and generateDependencyAttribution's outputDir provider (via the task's own output provider, not a bare path, so Gradle sees the producer/consumer edge) as unit-test task inputs, so editing a license document invalidates a cached green test result.
edge_cases: Build steps: JDK 17 temurin, ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest, lintDebug, assembleDebug; debug APKs uploaded with 14-day retention.

capabilities.name: SPDX header policy (docs/dev/spdx-header-policy.md)
capabilities.behavior: Identifier is `GPL-3.0-only` — explicitly NOT GPL-3.0-or-later and not the deprecated bare GPL-3.0. Copyright holder is the individual: `Copyright (C) 2026 Josh Engelbrecht`; "Lumose Health" and "GlycemicGPT" are org/project names, not legal entities, and must never appear as the holder. Canonical two-line block, verbatim, `//` for Kotlin/Java/Gradle KTS (above `package`), `#` for shell (after the shebang) and YAML (top). An existing descriptive block comment is kept and the SPDX lines go above it. In-scope globs: app/src, wear-device/src, watchface/src, plugins/pump-driver-api/src, plugins/example/src, plugins/shipped/tandem/src (all **/*.kt); the seven build.gradle.kts files and settings.gradle.kts listed INDIVIDUALLY (a recursive glob would reach excluded medtronic/spike build files); scripts/*.sh; .github/workflows/*.yml. Anything unmatched is not stamped. Exclusion beats inclusion where both match. LICENSE is never edited.
edge_cases: Out of scope by design: resource XML, AndroidManifest.xml, ProGuard rules, gradle.properties, shell.nix, renovate.json5, osv-scanner.toml, zizmor.yml, libs.versions.toml, contract/openapi.json, .githooks/*, lockfiles, build/ output, binaries, and ALL Markdown — prose carries its license via the repo LICENSE.

capabilities.name: SPDX never-stamp trees and the EcJpake attribution gap
capabilities.behavior: Normative exclusion list; a PR adding an upstream-derived file must add it to the list in the same PR. Objective test: excluded if upstream code was COPIED OR PORTED into it; in scope if upstream work was only STUDIED and reimplemented. When test and list disagree, treat as excluded and fix the list. Excluded: plugins/shipped/medtronic/** (whole tree, main and test — a direct OpenMinimed port; stated at directory level deliberately even though some di/ and plugin/ files are original, because file-by-file lines invite misattribution); tools/medtronic-ble-spike/**; gradlew, gradlew.bat, tools/medtronic-ble-spike/gradlew(.bat), gradle/wrapper/** (Gradle's own Apache-2.0 files — leave exactly as-is; do not add identifier lines to the ones lacking them). capabilities.name: PRIVACY.md — exact claims
capabilities.behavior: Scoped to android-unofficial (phone app, Wear OS face+companion, BLE driver plugins). The platform repo's docs/concepts/privacy.md is canonical and WINS on any conflict. Claims: nothing centralized; phone stores glucose/insulin in an encrypted Room database and tokens/credentials in EncryptedSharedPreferences; the watch keeps a small rolling cache of rendered values (recent glucose, trend, IoB) in app-private storage so the face survives restart, stores NO credentials, and requests NO internet permission. No telemetry; no distributed build sends health data or usage analytics. Exactly four outbound connections, all user-chosen: (1) the pump over BLE, direct and local; (2) your self-hosted backend if configured — with none configured the app still does local BLE monitoring, on-device storage and local threshold alerts with zero network calls; (3) the watch over the Wear OS Data Layer (Google Play Services transport — glucose, trend, IoB, alerts only, never credentials); (4) GitHub's release API, only on tapping "Check for updates", downloading from github.com / objects.githubusercontent.com. Last reviewed 2026-07-23.
edge_cases: Two third parties necessarily see connection/request metadata (Google Play Services, GitHub); neither receives health data.
Which AI provider processes data is determined by the user's backend config, not this app — the app never talks to AI providers directly.
Privacy concerns are reported through the SECURITY.md channels.

capabilities.name: PRIVACY.md — Sentry error-monitoring posture
capabilities.behavior: Sentry (donated via Sentry for Good) is used for the project's OWN development and CI only. The DSN is compiled in only when a developer supplies it at build time on their own machine (`SENTRY_DSN` env or `-PsentryDsn`); it is NEVER baked into any published APK — not signed release builds, not the CI-published `dev-latest` debug build. Release builds compile the DSN as an empty string and the build FAILS OUTRIGHT if a DSN is supplied to a CI build. Blank DSN = no-op integration. Configuration lockdown: error events only — no performance traces, no profiling, no session/release-health telemetry, no Session Replay, no screenshots or view-hierarchy capture, no user-interaction tracking; HTTP/navigation/UI/network automatic breadcrumbs dropped wholesale; every surviving string field passes a glucose/token/email scrubber; reporting IP replaced with a non-routable placeholder so Sentry cannot geo-locate. Report contents: stack trace, exception type, OS/runtime versions, app version and commit hash, triggering line. Never: glucose or health data, user identifiers/names/contacts, keys/tokens/credentials, device serials or pump pairing IDs, DB contents or query params, local variables, HTTP bodies, or health data interpolated into exception/log messages.
edge_cases: "Default -- nothing to opt out of": there is no project telemetry toggle because distributed builds carry no DSN.
Opting in sends reports to YOUR Sentry account, never the project's.

capabilities.name: MEDICAL-DISCLAIMER.md — regulatory status and no-write surface
capabilities.behavior: Disclaimer of record for this repo (phone app, Wear face/companion, Tandem+Medtronic drivers); the platform disclaimer governs backend/web/sidecar. Conflict rule: where a statement about this app or its device handling appears in both, THE STRICTER APPLIES; nothing in the platform disclaimer relaxes device-level limits. Not cleared/approved/certified by FDA, EU Notified Bodies (no CE marking under MDR 2017/745), Health Canada, TGA, or any equivalent. "NOT a medical device"; no person or entity is the "manufacturer" under any framework. No Therapeutic Write Surface: drivers READ glucose, IoB, basal, bolus history and pump hardware status and issue no therapeutic writes — no bolus dosing, no basal changes, no pump-setting modification; the plugin SDK has no insulin delivery primitives on any capability interface. Non-therapeutic device-management operations that DO exist (CGM calibration, BLE pair/unpair, connect/disconnect) are session/lifecycle operations, not therapy, and remain permitted. Any change introducing a therapeutic write would move the software into a regulatory category it is not built, tested, or licensed for. Last reviewed 2026-07-23.
edge_cases: Health data processed: CGM readings, pump telemetry (basal, bolus history, IoB), hardware status (battery, reservoir), user therapy parameters (target ranges, insulin ratios), meal entries, and food photos submitted for carb estimation.
AI analysis happens on the user's backend, not on the phone.

capabilities.name: MEDICAL-DISCLAIMER.md — warnings, forks, untested hardware, liability
capabilities.behavior: AI limitations named: hallucination, misinterpreting glucose data, outdated guidance, missing context (history, comorbidities, medications); all AI content labeled suggestions, not medical advice. Five Critical Warnings, including #4: alerts from this app depend on a BLE connection holding, Android scheduling background work, the watch being in range, and the phone being charged — they are a SUPPLEMENT to the pump's and CGM's own alerts, never a replacement, and device alerts must stay enabled. Project-owned unofficial builds are sideloaded from this repo's Releases page only; an APK from anywhere else is not covered. Third-party forks that add device control operate OUTSIDE the project — not reviewed, not recommended, no liability, and contributions intended to enable them are refused; users of such forks become the manufacturer of their personal medical device, following the Loop/AndroidAPS precedent. Untested-device clause: protocol compatibility does not guarantee correct operation; safety-critical values (IoB, glucose, basal) must always be verified against the manufacturer's official app; the README table is the authoritative per-device verification status.
edge_cases: Limitation of liability is stated in caps and then re-grounded in GPL-3.0 Sections 15/16/17.

Jurisdictional note: personal-injury liability limits may be unenforceable under EU consumer protection, UK consumer rights, and Australian consumer law; the project states its PRIMARY risk mitigation is the monitoring-only design, not the disclaimer.

capabilities.name: SECURITY.md — disclosure process
capabilities.behavior: Scope: this repo's phone app, Wear OS companion, and Tandem/Medtronic driver plugins; backend/web/sidecar go to the platform repo's policy. Do NOT open a public issue. Two private channels, both reaching the project lead: GitHub private vulnerability reporting (../../security/advisories/new) or security@glycemicgpt.org. If no response "within a few days", escalate via the channels in the platform repo's README. Required report contents: description and potential impact; reproduction steps or PoC; app version / commit SHA tested; whether the issue requires physical proximity to a BLE device. The project acknowledges, investigates, keeps the reporter updated, and asks for "a reasonable period" before public disclosure (no fixed embargo number is given). Supported versions: fixes land on `develop` and ship via the develop→main promotion; only the LATEST SIGNED RELEASE is supported — update before reporting.
edge_cases: No SLA numbers are committed to beyond "a few days" for first response.

capabilities.name: SECURITY.md — in-scope vulnerability classes (safety framing)
capabilities.behavior: Because the app has no therapeutic write surface, the named classes are: (1) INCORRECT BLE PARSING PRODUCING A WRONG GLUCOSE, IOB, OR DOSING-HISTORY VALUE — explicitly "a safety issue, not just a bug", report through this channel even though it isn't a classic security bug; (2) insecure local storage — glucose/insulin escaping the encrypted Room DB, or tokens escaping EncryptedSharedPreferences; (3) sensitive data in logs — pump serials, auth material, raw BLE payloads that could identify a device or user; (4) any code path that could introduce a therapeutic write primitive into a capability interface, even unintentionally; (5) standard app issues — insecure network calls to a configured backend, dependency vulnerabilities, unsafe deserialization, permission/intent handling. Monitoring-only posture is a DELIBERATE safety and legal boundary, not an implementation gap: a report proposing that the missing write capability is a bug to "fix" will be DECLINED as a feature request for a different, unendorsed kind of project.
edge_cases: No DAST or GitGuardian secret-scanning check exists in this repo's CI (no backend/web attack surface); GitGuardian-equivalent coverage is expected from GitHub platform Secret Scanning + Push Protection once the repo lives under the org.

capabilities.name: CONTRIBUTING — safety rules and device-driver contribution path
capabilities.behavior: "Safety First" non-negotiables: all AI outputs surfaced by the app must be labeled suggestions, not medical advice; test thoroughly because a wrong number on a glucose chart is a safety issue; safety limits (glucose range, max bolus, max basal) are platform-enforced via `SafetyLimits` and plugins MUST validate incoming pump and CGM history values against them — when a reading falls outside the limits the plugin must DISCARD it (do not return, emit, or persist) and LOG the rejection with the violated limit; no device control, full stop. Driver contribution steps: (1) pick an unsupported device; (2) open an issue naming device, protocol and data surfaced; (3) PR a Gradle module under plugins/shipped/<device-name>/ declaring only capabilities from the read-only enum — GLUCOSE_SOURCE, INSULIN_SOURCE, PUMP_STATUS, BGM_SOURCE, CALIBRATION_TARGET, BOLUS_CATEGORY_PROVIDER; (4) include unit tests, especially parsing and SafetyLimits validation; (5) runtime-loaded plugins under plugins/example/ are a separate advanced path, not compiled into official builds. Shipped drivers table: Tandem `:tandem-pump-driver` BLE central, "Stable -- reference implementation"; Medtronic `:medtronic-pump-driver` BLE peripheral advertise-and-wait, "Beta, read-only".

capabilities.name: CONTRIBUTING — DCO requirement
capabilities.behavior: Every commit must carry a `Signed-off-by: Name <email>` trailer certifying rights under the Developer Certificate of Origin. Use `git commit -s`; fix the last commit with `git commit --amend -s --no-edit`; multiple commits via interactive rebase or re-commit before pushing. Must use a REAL NAME and reachable email from git config, not an alias. Explicit rationale: DCO is a lightweight per-commit provenance attestation that does NOT grant the project relicensing rights; there is NO CLA. PRs with unsigned commits are blocked from merging until every commit in the branch carries a valid trailer. Server-side enforcement is the DCO GitHub App configured by .github/dco.yml: `require.members: true` (no exemption tier — maintainers and the project lead sign off like anyone else) and `allowRemediationCommits.individual: true` (one remediation commit, e.g. `git commit -s -m "chore: DCO remediation"`, can fix a whole PR's history instead of rewriting every commit).
edge_cases: The local commit-msg hook only WARNS on a missing sign-off; the App is authoritative and blocking.

capabilities.name: CONTRIBUTING — setup, branching, commits, and pre-submit checklist
capabilities.behavior: Prerequisites: phone app = JDK 17 + Android SDK Platform 35 (targetSdk 35, minSdk 30); Wear OS = JDK 17 + Platform 36 + Wear system image, phone and watch emulators paired via ADB. Quick start: fork, clone, `git remote add upstream`, install the hook (`cp .githooks/commit-msg .git/hooks/commit-msg && chmod +x`), `./gradlew assembleDebug`, `testDebugUnitTest`, `lintDebug`. Branching: develop/main. ALL contributor PRs target `develop`; never target `main`. Branch prefixes: feat/, fix/, docs/, refactor/, ci/. Conventional Commits drive release-please: feat, fix, perf, docs, refactor, ci are CHANGELOG-visible; chore and test are hidden. Pre-submit checklist: tests pass, lint clean with no new warnings, no hardcoded secrets/keys/tokens/credentials, new functionality has tests, Conventional Commit format, every commit signed off, branch up to date with develop. PR process: push branch, open PR against develop, fill the PR template completely, link issues with `Fixes #123` / `Relates to #123`; a code owner reviews and a maintainer squash-merges. Optional local pre-review via CodeRabbit CLI (`coderabbit review --plain --type uncommitted`).
edge_cases: GAP: CONTRIBUTING instructs contributors to "fill out the PR template completely", but this repository contains no .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE or .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE — every `../../issues/new/choose` link relies on org-level defaults.
Response expectation: PRs/issues answered "within a few days"; ping after a week.

capabilities.name: CONTRIBUTING — required CI checks and fork-PR handling
capabilities.behavior: Five required checks: Android Gate (unit tests, lint, debug APK for :app, :pump-driver-api, :tandem-pump-driver, :medtronic-pump-driver, :wear-device, :watchface); Security Scan Gate (Semgrep SAST on changed Kotlin); Dependency Scan Gate (OSV-Scanner over this repo's Gradle lockfiles); Attribution Check; Workflow Lint (zizmor on changed workflows, advisory while it beds in). Fork PRs run every required check with no maintainer action needed. Documented mechanism: the Attribution Check runs under `pull_request_target` so it executes in the base-repo context with a writable GITHUB_TOKEN, and it NEVER checks out PR code into the working tree — it fetches PR commits into a remote-only ref and inspects commit messages and diff text only (grep/sed), so it cannot install dependencies from the branch or execute pushed code. The Security Scan Gate runs Semgrep against the diff without building or running code, so it behaves identically for fork and branch PRs. CodeRabbit has its own review queue; stale state after rapid pushes is not a CI failure (`@coderabbitai review` re-triggers).
edge_cases: ci.yml is still a bootstrap smoke test that only proves GitHub App token minting works; it skips token steps for fork-originated pull_request runs because secrets are not passed to fork PRs.

capabilities.name: AI-attribution policy and its enforcement ladder
capabilities.behavior: Using AI to write code is fine; leaving AI attribution lines in the repo is not — the contributor owns, understands, and tests the code (AI is called out as especially prone to subtle BLE-parsing bugs). The full policy is org-wide. attribution-check.yml runs on pull_request_target for main/develop (opened, synchronize, reopened, edited), concurrency-grouped per PR with cancel-in-progress. Three layers: (1) commit trailers — a `Co-Authored-By: ...[bot]` not matching the whitelist is CRITICAL; a Co-Authored-By naming an AI tool without `[bot]` is HIGH; `Authored-By:`/`Generated-By:`/`AI-Generated-By:` are HIGH; (2) added lines in changed *.py/ts/tsx/js/jsx/kt/java/sh matching an attribution phrase plus a tool name or \bai\b/\bgpt\b are MEDIUM; (3) PR description matching AI branding is HIGH. Any severity != NONE exits 1. Bot whitelist (anchored to the start of the co-author name so "not really dependabot[bot]" cannot substring-match): github-actions, coderabbitai, glycemicgpt-security, glycemicgpt-ci, glycemicgpt-release, glycemicgpt-merge, glycemicgpt-renovate, dependabot, homebot-0, gitguardian.
edge_cases: CRITICAL AUTO-CLOSES the PR, skipped only when head ref is literally `develop` AND the head repo is this repository (guards against a fork branch named develop).

A sticky comment (marker `<!-- attribution-check-comment -->`) is upserted with paginated comment lookup; it is only posted when detect produced a severity, so an early crash cannot publish a misleading "Passed".
AI tool regex: claude|anthropic|copilot|chatgpt|openai|cursor|windsurf|codeium|codewhisperer|amazon.q|gemini|gemini.code.assist|jetbrains.ai|tabnine|sourcegraph|cody|devin|aider|codex.
CodeRabbit's auto-generated footer is stripped only when it is a properly bracketed block at the trailing end of the body — an earlier from-first-marker strip was a bypass.

capabilities.name: Local commit-msg hook (.githooks/commit-msg)
capabilities.behavior: One file, two jobs, because git runs only one commit-msg hook. Job 1: `sed -E -i.bak` deletes any `Co-Authored-By:` line matching the AI-tool alternation (Claude|Anthropic|Copilot|ChatGPT|OpenAI|Cursor|Windsurf|Codeium|CodeWhisperer|Amazon.Q|Gemini|JetBrains.AI|Tabnine|Sourcegraph|Cody|Devin|Aider|Codex|\[bot\]|noreply@, written with character classes for portable case handling), then deletes `Authored-By:`/`Generated-By:`/`AI-Generated-By:` trailers, then `perl -0777 -pi -e 's/\n{2,}\z/\n/'` collapses the trailing blank lines the strips leave. Job 2: if the message lacks a line matching `^Signed-off-by: .+ <.+@.+>$`, print a three-line WARNING to stderr (non-blocking) telling the author to use `git commit -s` and noting CI will block the PR. Always exits 0. Install via copy, or `git config core.hooksPath .githooks`.
edge_cases: Note the local hook's `noreply@` pattern is BROADER than the CI check, which deliberately does not treat a bare noreply@ as CRITICAL so a human co-author's PR is never auto-closed.

capabilities.name: ADR 0001 — API versioning and app-compatibility signal
capabilities.behavior: Status Accepted. Decision 1: LEAVE endpoint versioning AS-IS and document it. Only /api/v1/devices, /api/v1/alerts, /api/v1/api-keys and /api/v1/glucose/stream are version-prefixed; /api/auth, /api/settings, /api/ai, /api/food-records and most /api/integrations are unversioned. The split is historical, not designed; normalizing is a runtime backend change that would break every unversioned path the shipped app calls. If a breaking change to an unversioned path is unavoidable, introduce a /v2 sibling and keep the old path until the shipped fleet ages out — never mutate an unversioned path in place. Decision 2: design the compatibility signal now, implement later — backend exposes x-contract-version via an X-Contract-Version header on /health or a body field; the app pins the CONTRACT_VERSION it was built against, vendored at contract/CONTRACT_VERSION. CONTRACT_VERSION is a MONOTONICALLY INCREASING INTEGER starting at 1, compared numerically; anything unparseable or unreadable is treated as ABSENT, never silently as compatible.
edge_cases: SCOPED fail-open: signal present and app-required ≤ backend → proceed; signal older or absent/unparseable → proceed on READ/MONITORING paths with a one-time dismissible warning; individual failing calls handled per-call, never by blocking the app. Hard-refusing would brick a legitimate self-hoster.

EXPLICIT CARVE-OUT: were a therapeutic or safety-critical WRITE surface ever added, it must NOT inherit blanket fail-open — such an operation must be REFUSED when backend compatibility is unknown. Whole-app hard refusal is reserved for a future explicitly-declared hard-incompatibility epoch.

capabilities.name: ADR 0002 / ADR 0003 — tolerant reader and contract-drift strategy
capabilities.behavior: ADR 0002 (Accepted): the backend's tolerant-reader behavior IS the cross-cadence compatibility mechanism — legacy-value migration before validation (schemas/pump.py migrate_control_iq_mode rewrites legacy `standard` to `none` pre-validation; control_iq_mode is a loose str|None, not an enum) and loose-typed pass-through fields (raw_events, pump_info typed Any). Client half: Moshi DTOs ignore unknown keys, so additive drift is tolerated; a renamed/removed consumed field or a type change fails to parse. Only TWO directions are established: older app → newer backend, and newer backend → older app. Newer app → older backend is NOT proven compatible and is handled defensively per ADR 0001. ADR 0003 (Accepted): ContractSmokeTest is deliberately a smoke test, not a full DTO↔OpenAPI structural diff (disproportionate: would need a Kotlin-reflection + JSON-Schema resolver modeling @Json renames, nullability, Instant adapters, polymorphism). Pin refresh = copy platform apps/api/contract/openapi.json byte-for-byte and update contract/CONTRACT_VERSION.
edge_cases: KNOWN BLIND SPOT: round-trip tests catch removal of a required non-null undefaulted consumed field (Moshi throws) but silently tolerate removal of a nullable/defaulted one (deserializes to null). The exception is Nightscout pump_events[].units — nullable-consumed, and a null DROPS THE EVENT, UNDERSTATING IOB. It is covered by field-presence coupling (assertArrayItemFieldsPresent) instead. Rule: any new nullable consumed field whose absence would silently degrade a safety surface must be added to the field-presence coupling.

Recorded follow-up: consolidate the 20..500 bound into a single shared object; deliberately NOT bundled with the guard because it edits safety validators (require/init blocks in BgmReading, PluginEvent, EnrichedBolusEvent, CgmReading, SafetyLimits) and would enlarge the blast radius.

capabilities.name: CodeRabbit Medical-Safety review gate (.coderabbit.yaml)
capabilities.behavior: Three error-mode custom checks on every PR. "No Hardcoded Secrets": no keys, tokens, HMAC keys, passwords, keystore material, base64 secrets, committed .env values, private URLs/internal hostnames — credential leaks are critical severity in a health-tech app. "Medical Safety Review": glucose is STORED and COMPARED in canonical mg/dL — every persisted field, bound, threshold/alert comparison, dedup key and safety check must stay mg/dL and be bounds-checked to 20-500; mmol/L is display and input only; the single allowed factor is 18.0156. HARD-FAIL if code stores or compares an mmol/L value as mg/dL (e.g. persisting 3.9 instead of ~70 — "this silently suppresses low alerts"), converts the wrong direction, permits a stored mg/dL value outside 20-500 after conversion, or uses any other factor. It must NOT flag user-facing mmol/L display literals (3.9, 10.0, 22.2) or an mmol/L input converted before storage. Also verifies no auto-bolus/therapeutic device-command code exists and that AI suggestions carry safety disclaimers. "BLE Protocol Safety": GATT ops timed out and serialized, connection state transitions handled, LITTLE ENDIAN for Tandem, no raw pump data/serials/auth material logged at INFO.
edge_cases: Review tone is configured to ignore style, naming, and formatting and focus on correctness, security, medical safety, BLE protocol safety, and maintainability.
detekt and actionlint are enabled as CodeRabbit tools.

capabilities.behavior: Eight published pages under "Developer Reference", each with frontmatter, listed in a curated (non-alphabetical) order. instrumented-tests-ci — how the emulator-backed androidTest job runs in CI and how to run instrumented tests locally. security-testing — how security testing works in CI and how to extend it (also the reference for why Gradle lockfiles exist: OSV-Scanner does not parse build.gradle.kts or libs.versions.toml). dependency-updates — how Renovate proposes updates, which auto-merge, and the security policy behind it. release-and-promotion — how a develop→main promotion becomes a versioned release, changelog entry, and sync-back, plus the CI hygiene gates. signing-and-secrets — Android signing material stored in 1Password and loaded into GitHub Actions at runtime so no keystore or password is kept in GitHub. spdx-header-policy — covered above. plugin-architecture — developer reference for building mobile plugins. wear-os-architecture — the single phone-app-plus-watch-services architecture. edge_cases: These pages document Android/Gradle/GitHub-Actions mechanics that a Swift port will need equivalents for (signing, release promotion, dependency scanning), but their content was not read in depth in this pass.

safety_critical: docs/contract/safety-constants.md is the single source of truth for three cross-repo constants whose desync is a patient-safety failure: mmol↔mg/dL factor 18.0156, glucose-validity bound 20..500 mg/dL, Tandem epoch offset 1199145600 s (2008-01-01 UTC). Canonical storage is mg/dL everywhere; mmol/L is display-only (÷ 18.0156, round last); alert/SSE numerics stay mg/dL. Any change must land in both repos in the same coordinated release and update the page plus SafetyConstantDriftGuardTest's enumeration in the same PR.

The 20..500 bound has no single owner and is duplicated across ~17 shipped sites listed in safety-constants.md, including two documented off-by-one variants in AuthRepository.kt (20..499 and 21..500) and a SQL `BETWEEN 20 AND 500` in PumpDao.kt. A Swift port must consolidate rather than replicate the scatter, and must not lose the off-by-one sites silently.

CONTRIBUTING mandates the plugin-side validation behavior: a reading outside SafetyLimits must be DISCARDED — not returned, not emitted, not persisted — and the rejection logged with the violated limit. This is a hard rule for any Swift driver.

MEDICAL-DISCLAIMER Critical Warning #4 is an explicit alert-delivery non-guarantee: app alerts depend on the BLE connection holding, the OS scheduling background work, the watch being in range, and the phone being charged; they are a supplement to the pump's and CGM's own alerts, never a replacement, and device alerts must stay enabled. Any iOS port must carry this claim and must not strengthen it.

No therapeutic write surface anywhere: no bolus dosing, no basal rate changes, no pump-setting modification, and no insulin delivery primitive on any capability interface. Permitted non-therapeutic device-management ops are exactly CGM calibration, BLE pair/unpair, and connect/disconnect. This is asserted independently in MEDICAL-DISCLAIMER.md, SECURITY.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, README.md, and the CodeRabbit Medical Safety gate; SECURITY.md pre-declines any report proposing the boundary be 'fixed'.

ADR 0001's fail-open carve-out: monitoring/read paths fail open with a dismissible warning when backend compatibility is unknown, but a therapeutic or otherwise safety-critical write must be REFUSED under the same condition. If iOS ever adds such a surface it must not inherit the monitoring fail-open default.

ADR 0003 blind spot: removal of a nullable/defaulted consumed field is not caught by round-trip parsing. The known instance is Nightscout pump_events[].units — a null DROPS the event and UNDERSTATES IoB. Covered only by field-presence coupling to the pinned spec. Any new nullable consumed field that degrades a safety surface when absent must be added to that coupling.

SECURITY.md classifies incorrect BLE parsing that yields a wrong glucose, IoB, or dosing-history value as a security-channel report, not an ordinary bug — the private disclosure path must exist for wrong-number defects, not just classic vulnerabilities.

CodeRabbit's hard-fail list encodes the concrete conversion hazards: storing/comparing an mmol/L value as mg/dL (persisting 3.9 instead of ~70 silently suppresses low alerts), converting the wrong direction, permitting a stored mg/dL value outside 20-500 after conversion, or using a factor other than 18.0156.

Untested-hardware clause: Tandem Mobi is protocol-compatible but unverified on hardware, and Medtronic 680G/770G/780G is beta and unverified. Safety-critical values (IoB, glucose, basal) must always be verified against the manufacturer's official app. The README table is the authoritative per-device status the disclaimer defers to; an iOS port must publish its own equivalent table rather than inheriting this one.
Medtronic doc records that SmartGuard auto-basal micro-boluses are not yet fully attributed on the on-device read path — a known incompleteness in insulin display.

The in-app license viewer's Unavailable state exists only as a packaging failure signal; shipping an APK/IPA whose license section is blank is treated as a build-breaking defect (GradleException), not a runtime degradation.

map.notes:
SCOPE COVERAGE: all 20 markdown/mdx docs, all 7 _meta.json files, all 9 docs/licenses texts, notify-docs-update.yml, and all seven root policy documents were read in full. The eight docs/dev/ pages were read at frontmatter level plus spdx-header-policy.md in full (the only dev page that is legal-surface); their remaining content belongs to the CI/release, plugin, and Wear subsystem passes and is flagged as such rather than padded here. I followed the license pipeline out of docs into app/build.gradle.kts (both custom tasks in full), the root Licensee policy, the in-app viewer (LicensesScreen.kt, LicenseDocuments.kt, MarkdownText.kt), and its drift gate (LicenseAssetsTest.kt), plus the onboarding disclaimer gate, the attribution-check workflow, and the commit-msg hook, because those are where the docs' obligations are actually enforced.

KEY PORT-RELEVANT FINDINGS:
1. The website merges this repo's docs/ with the platform repo's docs/ into ONE namespace. Roughly a third of the relative links in published pages resolve only after that merge. An iOS docs tree must join the same namespace or rewrite every link.
2. Publication is gated by two hand-maintained things and nothing else: frontmatter (title + description) and membership in the section's _meta.json pages array. Nothing in CI validates either. The pages array is an explicit ORDER, not a filter over the directory.
3. The license pipeline is the strongest engineering constraint in this subsystem and must be rebuilt for iOS. Its non-negotiables: the shipped license screen reads GENERATED assets, never source strings; the component list comes from the resolved release dependency graph of EVERY module that ships a binary (four variants across three modules), so it cannot go stale; the build FAILS on an empty component list, an unclassified non-SPDX component, a blank source document, a missing README '## License' heading, or a license family with no bundled text. Licensee's allowlist is the other half of the gate. The iOS equivalent needs a generator over the resolved SwiftPM/CocoaPods graph plus a canonical-text bundle keyed by SPDX identifier, and an equivalent drift test.
4. Documented deliberate non-decisions worth preserving: EPL-1.0 is intentionally NOT allowlisted (FSF GPLv3 incompatibility) with the one offending transitive excluded at the dependency; docs/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md is deliberately NOT a runtime-dependency list; ADR 0003 deliberately chose a smoke test over a full DTO↔spec diff; the 20..500 consolidation is deliberately deferred because it edits safety validators; endpoint versioning is deliberately left un-normalized; display-only glucose clamps are deliberately outside the drift guard WITH a stated revisit trigger.
5. Open attribution gap to carry forward: EcJpake.kt is an Apache-2.0 port whose file carries no copyright notice and no license identifier, while Apache-2.0 requires the notice travel with the file. The SPDX policy names the exact header to add. If that file is ported to Swift, the notice must travel with it.
6. Gaps in this repo as of today: no .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE and no PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE despite CONTRIBUTING instructing contributors to fill the PR template; docs/dev/monorepo-port-ledger.md is referenced by CONTRIBUTING but absent; ci.yml is still a bootstrap smoke test whose own comment claims it is 'currently the only workflow in the repository' while 18 others exist; repo slugs are inconsistent across policy docs (GlycemicGPT/* vs lumose-health/*), so a port should pick one canonical org/slug before copying links.
7. Legal claims an iOS build must be able to keep truthfully: no telemetry in any distributed build (Sentry DSN empty in release, build FAILS if a DSN is supplied to CI); exactly four outbound connections, all user-chosen; watch stores no credentials and has no internet permission; no therapeutic write surface anywhere; GPL-3.0-only inbound=outbound with DCO and no CLA. Several of these are architecture commitments, not just prose.

ports_cleanly.ios_approach: SwiftUI. Settings → App Info → 'Open Source Licenses' row → NavigationStack destination titled 'Open Source Licenses' with a back affordance. Same three-state machine: Loading (ProgressView) → Loaded | Unavailable, with Unavailable showing 'License text could not be read from this build.' in the error color, treated as a packaging failure rather than a user state and logged. Loaded renders a ScrollView + LazyVStack with 16pt content padding and 12pt spacing, one row per paragraph so layout measures only on-screen content rather than ~670 GPL lines. .textSelection(.enabled) on the whole document replaces SelectionContainer. Scroll position preserved across rotation/scene restoration via @SceneStorage on a scroll anchor. Documents read from Bundle.main off the main actor; no connectivity required.

Three rules port unchanged. (1) Repository-relative links are reduced to their label text because such a path addresses a file that does not exist on device; targets carrying a URI scheme (including mailto:) are left intact even if the renderer declines to open them. (2) The generated component document splits at '## ' boundaries with the heading kept in its section and the preamble as section 0. (3) License texts and the GPL are rendered as PLAIN TEXT, never markdown — numbered clauses parse as list markers and indented lines as code blocks. On iOS: Text(verbatim:) for plain-text documents, AttributedString(markdown:) only for the notice and component documents, image syntax stripped, data detectors and automatic link detection OFF so 'some-file.md' is not linkified, and only http/https targets openable.

XCTest reading the built bundle's licenses/ resources back and comparing against on-disk sources. Keep every assertion: shipped GPL text == repo LICENSE verbatim and >30,000 chars containing 'GNU GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE' and 'Version 3, 29 June 2007'; shipped third-party == docs/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md verbatim, >10,000 chars, starting '# Third-Party Licenses'; project notice >200 chars, starts '## License', is a verbatim substring of README.md, contains no later '\n## ' (over-capture guard), and contains both 'Copyright (C) 2026 Josh Engelbrecht' and 'GPL-3.0-only'; component asset starts '# Redistributed Components' and names a fixed witness set including at least one watch-only package; heading-set closure against declared SPDX and non-SPDX heading sets; section-split count == '## ' line count + 1; non-blank UPSTREAM NOTICES block with a named stable witness package.

Both output documents are plain text and port unchanged. runtime_dependencies.md: '# Redistributed Components', three fixed preamble paragraphs, 'Components: <N>.', then one '## <heading>' per license family sorted alphabetically where the heading is the component's first license identifier or the literal 'License terms available elsewhere'; each entry '- `identity` -- <name> -- carries a NOTICE' (name omitted when blank or equal to the identity, NOTICE suffix only when that component contributed one), then an indented scm URL line, then 'Also licensed under: X, Y', then 'Terms: <note>'. runtime_dependency_licenses.txt: 'LICENSE TEXTS AND UPSTREAM NOTICES' header, per identifier a 64-'=' separator / identifier / separator / bundled text, then a final 'UPSTREAM NOTICES' block of '--- identity ---' sections. De-duplicate by package identity so multi-target/multi-platform resolution collapses.

The four-step fallback ports exactly: declared SPDX identifier → unmapped override → external-terms note → build failure. Two rules are load-bearing and must survive: the override is consulted ONLY when nothing was declared (a declared identifier always wins), and a component that is neither declared nor classified is a build failure, never an 'undeclared' placeholder. Contents change wholesale — Swift packages frequently ship a LICENSE file with no machine-readable declaration, so the unmapped map will be LARGER on iOS than on Android. The unreproduced map retains the pattern for terms that live elsewhere (Apple frameworks are first-party and out of scope; any GPL-3.0 Swift Medtronic module gets the same 'the license this application ships under' note).

needs_redesign.why: There is no app.cash.licensee for Swift. A standalone Swift executable in a Tools/ package invoked as an Xcode pre-build script and from CI
LicensePlist as an off-the-shelf tool

Reject option 3: LicensePlist does not fail the build on an unclassified component, cannot enforce the no-empty-component-list rule, and has no policy allowlist — the fail-closed behavior IS the requirement here, not the file generation. Resolution must be strict, never lenient — a failure breaks the build rather than silently dropping a NOTICE. It must cover EVERY target that ships in a binary (phone app, watch app, widget/complication extension, and every driver target), not just the phone app, because the Android pipeline's lesson is that five of six reproduced NOTICE files were reachable only through the watch module.

Preserve the rest of the behavior exactly: multiple notices within one package sorted by path and joined with a blank line; empty or whitespace-only notices dropped; an unreadable checkout raising a hard error rather than silently dropping attribution; the notices map sorted by package identity; and a named stable witness package asserted by the drift test so a silent regression to zero notices is impossible.

One local Swift package per device consumed as a path dependency

Preserve verbatim: the read-only capability set as Swift protocols (GLUCOSE_SOURCE, INSULIN_SOURCE, PUMP_STATUS, BGM_SOURCE, CALIBRATION_TARGET, BOLUS_CATEGORY_PROVIDER) with nothing else declarable; the hard SafetyLimits rule that a reading outside the limits must be DISCARDED — not returned, not emitted, not persisted — and the rejection LOGGED with the violated limit; unit tests required, especially on parsing and limits validation; the refusal to merge PRs introducing therapeutic write primitives and the refusal of contributions whose intent is to enable a device-control fork. ADD a step the Android page has no need for and which is now mandatory: a driver PR must name who will validate it on physical hardware and on which device, because Simulator validation cannot exercise BLE at all. Ship a simulated driver so parser correctness stays testable without hardware.

needs_redesign.capability: CONTRIBUTING — setup, branching, commits, pre-submit checklist
needs_redesign.why: Prerequisites, build commands and local gate reproduction are entirely different toolchain. JDK 17 + Android SDK 35/36 + paired phone and watch emulators become macOS + Xcode + Simulator runtimes; ./gradlew assembleDebug / testDebugUnitTest / lintDebug become xcodebuild invocations.
options: Direct substitution of prerequisites and commands
Substitution plus a Makefile or script wrapper so one command reproduces each CI gate locally
needs_redesign.recommendation: Option 2 — the Android page's most useful property is that a contributor can reproduce every gate locally, and a wrapper is what preserves it across a much noisier toolchain. Prerequisites become macOS 15+, Xcode 16+, a Swift 6 toolchain, and iOS 18 / watchOS 11 Simulator runtimes. Branching, commits and the checklist port unchanged: develop and main, ALL contributor PRs target develop and never main, branch prefixes feat/ fix/ docs/ refactor/ ci/, Conventional Commits driving release-please with feat/fix/perf/docs/refactor/ci changelog-visible and chore/test hidden, and the pre-submit checklist (tests pass, lint clean with no new warnings, no hardcoded secrets, new functionality has tests, Conventional Commit format, every commit signed off, branch up to date with develop).
